I'm 74 years old this year, and I've been farming these same fields in Quzhou for half a century. My legs aren't what they used to be, but I know every corner of my 6 mu. My son works over at a factory in Handan — he sends back about 2,000 yuan a month, which helps with the household. My wife and daughter-in-law are here to help with the farm work, and my grandson pitches in on weekends when school allows. But cotton picking season is brutal, so we hire a few local women to help, pay them by the jin.

I keep 3 mu in cotton, same as always. The other 3 mu I do wheat and then maize right after — double cropping. The wheat went in last October with our regular local variety. I put down base fertilizer then — about 25 kg of compound fertilizer per mu. Now it's April and the wheat is greening up nicely. I need to topdress with urea soon, around Qingming. I'll spread about 6–7 kg of urea per mu, which brings my total nitrogen to about 14 kg per mu. The extension fellow told me last year I ought to push it to 18 kg, but 14 has given me decent crops for decades and fertilizer prices have gone up again. Last year I got about 420 kg/mu on that field. This year I reckon 400 kg/mu is fair — the soil looks about average. I'll irrigate twice from the well: once now at green-up, and again at grain filling if June turns dry. Pumping costs me about 40 yuan each time, so I don't water unless it's needed.

For cotton, I plant in mid-to-late April. I saved my own seed from the batch I bought two years ago — it's a local improved type, not the expensive hybrid seed, but it's reliable and I know how it behaves. Before planting I'll plow and harrow the field. I put compound fertilizer in the planting furrow, about 20 kg/mu, and then topdress with urea at first flowering, another 5 kg/mu or so. Total nitrogen works out to roughly 12 kg/mu. I irrigate three times: right after planting to help it settle, again at flowering, and once more at the boll stage. The bollworm is my main worry every year — I'll spray insecticide twice and lay down herbicide once before planting. Cotton is a money crop but it eats labor. Between planting, managing, and picking spread across September and October, my family puts in about 30 days on those 3 mu, and I hire another 8 days of help for the peak picking. Last year I got about 250 kg/mu of lint after all the ginning. I'm hoping for the same this year if the weather holds.

The maize goes in right after wheat harvest, around June 15th. At my age I can't turn around a double-crop by hand in less than a week, so I hire Old Wang's tractor to rotary-till and plant in one go. I use hybrid seed for maize — the yield difference is big enough that it's worth the extra cost. One shot of compound fertilizer at planting, about 25 kg/mu, gives me roughly 13 kg of nitrogen. I might irrigate once at the silking stage, maybe twice if it's a dry summer, but maize is tough and I don't baby it. I expect about 450 kg/mu. For labor, it's light — about 6 family days total and 2 hired days for the custom planting.

Money is always tight. My total cash outlay for seeds, fertilizer, pesticide, pumping, and hired labor across all three crops this year comes to about 1,520 yuan. That's a big chunk of our flexible income. I thought about cutting back on cotton fertilizer to save money, but if I under-fertilize and the yield drops, I lose more than I save. I'd rather spend a bit extra on fertilizer than risk a bad year — I've seen what a bad year does to a family.
